subject: Rate card question: are prefix-cache hits charged against baseline tokens?
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@atlas.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick clarifying question on cache billing

Hi Karthik,

We're reviewing the rate card and want to be precise about how prefix/prompt caching is accounted for in hosted API billing. We have an example I'd like confirmed so we can model costs into our POC budget:

Example: user prompt = 150 tokens. Model generates a continuation of 300 tokens. In our workload ~100 tokens at the start of the prompt are identical across many requests and would be satisfied by Redwood's prefix cache.

Question: when the prefix cache returns the first 100 tokens without touching the model, does Atlas get billed for those 100 prompt tokens as part of baseline/metered tokens, or only for the tokens that actually hit the model (the remaining 50 prompt + 300 generated = 350)?

Also: does this behavior change if the model variant changes (e.g., switching from gptx-3-small to gptx-3-large) or if we enable a deduplication policy?

We want to be explicit in our internal rate model and in the upcoming SOW. Appreciate a short, clear answer we can include in the procurement sheet.

Thanks,
Tom
--
Tom Blake
Head of Applied ML, Atlas AI
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@atlas.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: 2026-03-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifying question on cache billing

Tom — thanks, great (and specific) question. I'm looping in product to give the definitive answer, but short summary up front: we only bill tokens that traverse the model runtime. If a prefix is served entirely from a persistent prefix cache (no model compute), those cached prompt tokens are not billed. There are some nuance bullets below and a quick example with numbers. Attaching the current rate card for reference.

Action: marissa, david — can you confirm wording and any exceptions we should flag to procurement?

--
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Fwd: Quick clarifying question on cache billing (Atlas example)

Marissa / David — forwarding Tom's example. Key asks: 1) Are prefix cache hits excluded from metered prompt tokens on hosted API rate card? 2) Any caveats around model variant changes, cache eviction / TTL, and dedupe? 3) Would this be something to call out in the SOW / contract language?

I attached the rate card PDF we already shared with them. They want a sentence we can copy into procurement.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-30T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick clarifying question on cache billing (Atlas example)

Hey team — here is the product-legal-friendly wording and the detailed behavior. Please use the first paragraph for procurement; the bullets are for internal nuance.

Short answer for procurement (one-liner to drop into SOW):
"Redwood bills only for tokens that require model execution. Tokens fully satisfied from Redwood's prefix/prompt cache are not charged on an inference invoice; billed tokens equal the sum of non-cached prompt tokens and generated tokens that pass through the model runtime."

Detailed notes / caveats:
- Cache scope: The prefix cache is keyed by (model_name, model_version, prefix_digest, tenant_id, cache_policy). If any of those differ (e.g., switching model_version), the cache entry is not eligible and the tokens will be re-computed and billed.
- Partial hits: If part of the prompt is served from cache and the rest must be executed, only the non-cached prompt tokens are billed. In your example: prompt 150 tokens with first 100 cache-hit -> billed prompt tokens = 50. Generated tokens (300) are billed if they are produced by model execution. Total billed tokens = 350 in that scenario.
- Deduplication / normalization: If you enable dedupe/prefix-normalization, the cache hit rate may change; the above billing rule still applies (only non-cached tokens billed).
- Model fallback/compatibility: If a request is routed to a different compatible model (policy fallback), and the cache is not shared across that model variant, the request will be billed as if uncached. We recommend customers pin model_version in workloads where cache-sensitive economics are critical.
- Visibility & metrics: Console exposes cache_hit_token_count and cache_miss_token_count per request (per-route). Customers can use these metrics to reconcile billing. We also provide a CSV export of per-route token breakdowns on request (see attached example-usage-logs.csv).
- Edge cases (billing): Very short cached prefixes used only for reranking or signal enrichment are still accounted for by the same rules; we do not bill cached traffic that never touches the model.

If you want exact numbers for your expected QPS/ratio we can run a small simulation using your sample traces. Happy to add the procurement wording to the SOW and include a note about pinning model version to preserve cache economics.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@atlas.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-30T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarifying question on cache billing

Tom — thanks for the clear example. Here is the short, copy-pasteable statement you can include in procurement:

"Redwood bills only for tokens that require model execution. Tokens fully satisfied from Redwood's prefix/prompt cache are not charged on an inference invoice; billed tokens equal the sum of non-cached prompt tokens and generated tokens that pass through the model runtime."

For your numbers: prompt 150 (100 cached) + generated 300 -> billed tokens = 50 + 300 = 350. If you switch model_version and the cache is not shared, you will be billed for all 450 tokens.

Next steps: if you want, we can (a) run a 72-hour replay of a representative trace and send an estimated cost delta, or (b) include the above language in the SOW and add a clause recommending pinning model_version for cache-sensitive endpoints. Which would you prefer?

I can book 30 minutes this week to walk through the rate card vs your forecast.

Cheers,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
